- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% to offset overconfidence.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model often averages out extremes; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
